Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html`.

- Dark-styled page, title "CHIP-8 Emulator".

- memory: Uint8Array(4096). Load the standard CHIP-8 font set (16 digits 0-F, 5 bytes each) at address 0x050. Standard font bytes:

- V: Uint8Array(16) registers; I: 16-bit index; pc starting at 0x200; stack: array of 16-bit return addresses (with sp); delayTimer, soundTimer counting down at 60 Hz (decrement in the requestAnimationFrame loop based on elapsed time, or once per frame at 60fps); keypad: array of 16 booleans.
- Display buffer: Uint8Array(64*32).
- Complete 35-instruction decode/execute in a step() method:
  00E0 CLS; 00EE RET; 0nnn SYS nnn (treat as no-op); 1nnn JP; 2nnn CALL; 3xkk SE Vx,byte; 4xkk SNE Vx,byte; 5xy0 SE Vx,Vy; 6xkk LD Vx,byte; 7xkk ADD Vx,byte (no carry flag); 8xy0 LD; 8xy1 OR; 8xy2 AND; 8xy3 XOR; 8xy4 ADD with VF=carry; 8xy5 SUB with VF=NOT borrow (VF=1 if Vx>=Vy); 8xy6 SHR (VF = LSB of Vx before shift, Vx >>= 1); 8xy7 SUBN (Vx = Vy - Vx, VF = NOT borrow, VF=1 if Vy>=Vx); 8xyE SHL (VF = MSB of Vx before shift, Vx <<= 1); 9xy0 SNE Vx,Vy; Annn LD I,nnn; Bnnn JP V0+nnn; Cxkk RND Vx = random & kk; Dxyn DRW: draw n-byte sprite from memory[I] at (Vx,Vy), each byte a row of 8 pixels, XOR onto screen, wrap coordinates modulo 64/32, VF=1 if any set pixel was unset (collision), else 0; Ex9E SKP (skip if key Vx pressed); ExA1 SKNP (skip if key Vx NOT pressed); Fx07 LD Vx,DT; Fx0A LD Vx,K (wait for key press — block by not advancing pc until a key is pressed, then store the key index); Fx15 LD DT,Vx; Fx18 LD ST,Vx; Fx1E ADD I,Vx (I += Vx); Fx29 LD I = font address of digit Vx (0x050 + Vx*5); Fx33 BCD: store hundreds/tens/ones of Vx at memory[I], [I+1], [I+2]; Fx55 LD [I..I+x] = V0..Vx (classic: I left unchanged or incremented — use I unchanged variant, document choice); Fx65 LD V0..Vx = [I..I+x].
- Unknown opcode: throw/log an error and halt.
- Sound: when soundTimer > 0, play a beep using WebAudio (create AudioContext lazily on first user gesture; include a mute/sound toggle button that works).
- Main loop: requestAnimationFrame; when running, execute `instructionsPerFrame` opcodes per frame, then decrement timers at 60Hz and redraw canvas only when display changed (or every frame — simple is fine).
- reset(): clear memory/registers/stack/display/timers, reload font, pc=0x200.
- loadRom(bytes): reset then copy bytes at 0x200.

=== DISASSEMBLER ===
A function disassemble(opcode) returning a human string for the debugger panel, covering all 35 instructions (e.g. 0x8xy4 -> "ADD Vx, Vy", 0xD015 -> "DRW V0, V1, 5", unknown -> "??? 0x....").

On page load, automatically load this demo ROM (paused) so the emulator is immediately usable; show a short on-screen hint: "Press Run, then use 2/4/6/8 (W/A/S/D also work per the keypad map) to move the alien."

keydown/keyup listeners on window; ignore repeats (e.repeat); map per the table above; both press and release update emulator keypad state and the visual keypad highlight. preventDefault for mapped keys so the page doesn't scroll.
